ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the graph of the linear function $y=kx+b$ intersects the $x$ axis at point $A(3, 0)$ and intersects the $y$ axis at point $B(0, 4)$. It intersects the graph of the direct proportion function $y=ax$ at point $C$, and the $x$-coordinate of point $C$ is 2. What is the solution set of the inequality $0<kx+b<ax$?
ready1_open_rewrite.title: MM-Math open-ended problem
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: As shown in the figure, the graph of the linear function $y=kx+b$ intersects the $x$-axis at point $A(3,0)$ and the $y$-axis at point $B(0,4)$. It intersects the graph of the direct proportion function $y=ax$ at point $C$, and the $x$-coordinate of point $C$ is 2. What is the solution set of the inequality $0<kx+b<ax$?
ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer: Substitute $A(3,0)$ and $B(0,4)$ into $y=kx+b$ to get: \[ \begin{cases} b=4\\ 3k+b=0 \end{cases} \] Solving gives $b=4$ and $k=-\frac{4}{3}$, so the equation of the linear function is $y=-\frac{4}{3}x+4$. Substituting $x=2$ into $y=-\frac{4}{3}x+4$ gives $y=\frac{4}{3}$, so point $C$ is $\left(2,\frac{4}{3}\right)$. Substituting $C$ into $y=ax$ gives $a=\frac{2}{3}$, so the equation of the direct proportion function is $y=\frac{2}{3}x$. Thus the inequality becomes $0<-\frac{4}{3}x+4<\frac{2}{3}x$. From the graph, the solution set is $2<x<3$. Hence, the answer is $\boxed{2<x<3}$.

再推理：不等式 0<kx+b<ax 表示直线 y=kx+b 的函数值要大于 0，也就是在 x 轴上方；同时它还要小于 y=ax，也就是位于直线 y=ax 的下方。由图和题意可知，y=kx+b 在 A(3,0) 处等于 0，并且这条直线向右下降，所以 y=kx+b>0 对应 x<3。两条直线在 C 点相交，题给 C 的横坐标为 2；从图上看，在 C 的右侧，向上倾斜的直线 y=ax 位于向下倾斜的直线 y=kx+b 上方，所以 kx+b<ax 对应 x>2。合并两个条件，得到 2<x<3。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, the graph of the linear function $y=kx+b$ intersects the $x$-axis at point $A(3,0)$ and the $y$-axis at point $B(0,4)$. It intersects the graph of the direct proportion function $y=ax$ at point $C$, and the $x$-coordinate of point $C$ is 2. What is the solution set of the inequality $0<kx+b<ax$?
raw_record.answer:
Substitute $A(3,0)$ and $B(0,4)$ into $y=kx+b$ to get:
\[
\begin{cases}
b=4\\
3k+b=0
\end{cases}
\]
Solving gives $b=4$ and $k=-\frac{4}{3}$, so the equation of the linear function is $y=-\frac{4}{3}x+4$.

Substituting $x=2$ into $y=-\frac{4}{3}x+4$ gives $y=\frac{4}{3}$, so point $C$ is $\left(2,\frac{4}{3}\right)$.

Substituting $C$ into $y=ax$ gives $a=\frac{2}{3}$, so the equation of the direct proportion function is $y=\frac{2}{3}x$.

Thus the inequality becomes $0<-\frac{4}{3}x+4<\frac{2}{3}x$. From the graph, the solution set is $2<x<3$. Hence, the answer is $\boxed{2<x<3}$.
raw_record.final_cot:
First describe the image: In the figure there is a plane rectangular coordinate system, the horizontal axis is the x-axis, and the vertical axis is the y-axis. A straight line inclined downward to the right represents the linear function y=kx+b; it passes through point B on the positive semi-axis of the y-axis and point A on the positive semi-axis of the x-axis. Another straight line inclined upward to the right passes through the origin O, representing the direct proportional function y=ax. The two straight lines intersect at point C in the first quadrant.

Then reason: According to the problem, A(3,0) and B(0,4) are on the linear function y=kx+b. Substituting B(0,4), obtain b=4. Substituting A(3,0), obtain 3k+b=0, so 3k+4=0, solving gives k=-4/3. Therefore the linear function is y=-4x/3+4.

The abscissa of point C is 2, and C is on the linear function, so y_C=-4/3×2+4=-8/3+12/3=4/3, therefore C=(2,4/3). Also C is on the direct proportional function y=ax, so 4/3=2a, solving gives a=2/3.

The original inequality 0<kx+b<ax becomes 0<-4x/3+4<2x/3. Solve separately: -4x/3+4>0 gives x<3; -4x/3+4<2x/3 gives 4<2x, namely x>2. Taking the intersection of the two, obtain 2<x<3.
